c.tagline: Guizhou's karst heartland and gateway to Huangguoshu, China's largest waterfall, with Ming-garrison Tunpu villages and masked Dixi opera.

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis are common in the city, and Didi is the easiest way to book a car; for the waterfall and Tunpu villages, hiring a car for the day or joining a tour is usually simpler than piecing together buses.

emergency.note: 120 is the ambulance number, 119 is fire and 110 is police. English is rarely spoken, so a translation app or your destination written in Chinese is very helpful.

hood_landmark.Xixiu (City Center): Anshun Ancient City Gufu Snack Street

hood_desc: The compact old core of Anshun in Xixiu District, centred on the restored Anshun Ancient City, the Confucius Temple and the lively Gufu snack street; the practical, walkable base with the best spread of restaurants, markets and mid-range hotels.

The city's green centrepiece, a landscaped lake and lakeside park ringed by newer four- and five-star hotels beside the municipal offices; a calmer, scenic base with hot springs nearby and easy access to the train station and airport.

The scenic-area town about 45 km southwest, strung along the approach to the thundering 78-metre Huangguoshu Waterfall and the linked Tianxingqiao and Doupotang cascades; a nature-focused base for those who want to catch the falls at first light before the crowds.

The modern transport hub around the high-speed Anshun West Railway Station, with convenient chain hotels a short walk from the platforms; a functional base for early trains to Guiyang and Kunming or a night before heading to the airport.

A 600-year-old Ming military garrison village about 30 km east toward Pingba, where descendants of Han soldiers still wear Fengyang dress, live in stone courtyard houses and perform the masked wooden-relic Dixi 'ground opera'; a cultural, slow-paced spot best visited by day.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM; after that use Didi or a taxi, especially to reach the high-speed station or the scenic areas outside town.
transit.note: Anshun has no metro; getting around means city buses, Didi, taxis and walking in the compact centre. The big sights - Huangguoshu, Dragon Palace and the Tunpu villages - lie well outside town and are reached by tourist coaches, chartered cars or day tours.
transit.pay: Pay city buses in exact-change cash or, more commonly, by scanning with Alipay or WeChat Pay; foreign visitors should set up mobile pay in advance, as it is now the default.

landmarks: Longgong (Dragon Palace) Caves
China's longest water-filled cave system, where boats glide through cathedral-like karst caverns of technicolour-lit stalactites and an underground waterfall.
Tianxingqiao Scenic Area
Huangguoshu's enchanting sister site, a wonderland of stone forests, pothole pools, and bridges culminating in the silvery braids of Yinlianzhui Falls.
Doupotang Waterfall
The widest cascade in the Huangguoshu group, a 105-metre curtain of water whose deep rumble earned it the name 'Roaring Falls'.
Tianlong Tunbao Ancient Town
A living Ming-dynasty garrison village where Tunbao descendants preserve 600-year-old stone architecture, costumes, and masked dixi opera.
Yunfeng Tunpu (Eight Villages)
A cluster of fortified Ming-era garrison villages beneath Yunjiu Mountain, their stone watchtowers and courtyards frozen in 14th-century military life.
Anshun Confucian Temple (Wen Miao)
A remarkably preserved 1394 temple complex whose transparently carved dragon columns rank among the finest stone sculpture in southwest China.
Anshun Batik Museum
The best introduction to Anshun's title as China's 'batik capital', displaying exquisite indigo wax-resist textiles of the Miao and Buyi peoples.
Guanling National Geopark
A day-trip fossil treasury preserving spectacular Triassic marine reptiles and sea lilies, evidence of the ancient ocean that once covered Guizhou.
Hongshan Lake
The largest lake in downtown Anshun, a landscaped waterfront where locals walk, fish and relax beneath pavilions and willow-lined paths in the heart of the city.
Jiuzhou Old City
The original walled city center of Anshun, a warren of narrow flagstone alleys and timber houses that has kept its traditional look for centuries.

train.note: Anshun has no international trains. From Anshun West Railway Station on the Shanghai-Kunming high-speed line, trains reach Guiyang in about 30 minutes and Kunming in around 2 hours, making Anshun an easy add-on to a wider Guizhou or Yunnan trip; the older Anshun station in town still handles slower conventional services. Tickets are sold on 12306 with your passport (foreign passport holders can also book through Trip.com), and seats on the Guiyang-Kunming corridor sell out over Chinese public holidays.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Anshun. Buses and tourist coaches from the city run to Guiyang (about 1.5 hours), the Huangguoshu and Longgong scenic areas, and out to the Tunpu villages and Getu River, the usual way to reach the sights beyond the reach of the railway. Tickets are bought at the terminal counter or on Chinese travel apps; the nearest cross-border coaches leave from Nanning, several hours away by train.

ferry.note: Anshun is deep inland in the Guizhou highlands and has no passenger ferry services. The only boats are short sightseeing trips inside the Longgong (Dragon Palace) cave system and on the reservoirs near Huangguoshu, sold as part of the scenic-area ticket.

half.name: Huangguoshu Waterfall
half.blurb: China's largest waterfall, a 78-metre curtain nearly 100 metres wide that you can walk behind through the Water-Curtain Cave, set in a cluster of cascades linked by the Tianxingqiao scenic trail.

half.name: Dragon Palace (Longgong)
half.blurb: A spectacular karst cave system about 28 km south where you glide by boat through China's longest water-filled cave beneath shimmering stalactites, alongside waterfalls and a serene karst lake.

half.name: Tianlong Tunpu
half.blurb: A 600-year-old stone garrison village where Ming soldiers' descendants keep their Fengyang dress, courtyard homes and haunting masked Dixi 'ground opera' alive.

full.name: Getu River National Park
full.blurb: A dramatic karst gorge in Ziyun, famous for its colossal Great Arch cave, free-solo climbers, cliff-dwelling caves and boat rides through soaring limestone scenery.

full.name: Zhijin Cave
full.blurb: One of China's grandest show caves, a vast underground palace of cathedral-sized chambers and towering formations, roughly two hours north of Anshun.

full.name: Guiyang
full.blurb: Guizhou's mountain capital, with the riverside Jiaxiu Pavilion, the sprawling Qingyan ancient town and some of the province's best Miao and Dong food, about 30 minutes away by high-speed train.
